doc.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-10-07

title: De De's teacher Charlot and his influences
summary: He learned his notes from Charlot, a letter carrier, was influenced by Rene and Chris Kelly, and picked up mute playing himself.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: And when he wasn't busy he was resting at home. I left my wife and tell me, you know, one of those things, you know, resting or so. So I left him and I went to a fellow we called Charlotte and he was a letter carrier, he was an old man. St. Claude, I think he was in the main. He used to teach, you know, teach music, all instruments. And I learned mostly my notes from Charlotte. And I began to sprout around from one little outfit to the other. One when they need to sit in, you know, man to sit in, man is a trumpet player, well he send me in his place. Mostly all the old heads, when I began to play a little, pull it high extra, you know, extra man, or when they need the trumpet player, I was in their places like that. That's how I got my stuff.
Well who did you, you developed your style along? Anybody influenced you?
Well I imagine Rene did. I imagine the first one. I liked his playing.
Uh huh. And what about, uh, with the mutes? Did you get your mute style from anybody?
No, no, no, no. I just picked that up mostly myself. Uh huh. Gotta go to the store and try, you know, what I imagine sounds good to me, you know. That's what I imagine.
What about Chris Kelly? Do you think he had any influence on you?

Yeah, he worked a lot of blues. I wish he was a blues man, you know. Uh huh. Do you know his blues today, any of them? Oh, it's so many. It's another thing. He played so much with himself. Careless, love, and all those other numbers like that.
Oh yeah, he'll be, he'll be. Uh, did you have any other teachers besides Rene and Charlene?
Well, no, no. Outside of Paul Barnes, well that was the way we were late years after. Cause we had an opposite together. Paul taught me a lot, you know. I see.
